subject: Post-call: POC success matrix, model picks, and multilingual scope
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC success matrix and model picks

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation and clear priorities from your side. Below is a concise recap and proposed trial plan so we can confirm scope and owners.

Quick recap of Nimble Retail priorities
- Multilingual product FAQ assistant (EN, ES, PT-BR)
- Low-latency conversational responses for chat widgets (95th pctile < 600ms server-side)
- High hallucination resistance for price/sku lookups and returns policy language
- Measurable business success: reduction in CS deflection volume and faster resolution time

Proposed POC objective (4 weeks):
- Deliver a working inference integration in staging that answers product and returns questions in EN/ES/PT-BR with acceptable accuracy and latency.

Success criteria (pass/fail gating):
1) Quality: >= 80% helpfulness in blinded human eval on a 200-prompt test set (sample attached: test_prompt_suite.csv) across the three languages, and BLEU/BERTScore thresholds we can agree on during scoping.
2) Latency: 95th percentile server-side token latency < 600ms for typical sessions (average prompt length ~60 tokens).
3) Stability: no more than 1% server errors during a 48-hour soak run at expected QPS.
4) Safety: No policy-violating outputs in a 500-prompt safety sweep.
5) Business signal: pilot channel shows >= 15% reduction in repeat CS tickets for the tested flows (tracked post-deploy).

Model recommendations for the trial
- Primary: Mistral-7b-Instruct (quantized) as a high-throughput baseline for EN + PT-BR (good latency/cost tradeoff).
- Conversational fallback / quality candidate: OpenAssistant-13B-v2-chat (unquantized) for higher-quality responses when route policy permits slightly higher latency.
- Safety fallback: Llama-2-13b-chat (fine-tuned safety prompts) as a last-resort deterministic fallback for policy-critical queries.

Routing policy suggestion: preferentially serve Mistral-7b for standard queries; escalate to OA-13B for ambiguous/longer prompts or where higher precision is required; route high-risk or policy queries to Llama-2-13b-chat with strict post-processing.

Operational owners (proposed)
- Redwood commercial lead: Marissa Cole (day-to-day coordination)
- Redwood solutions eng: Rishi Malhotra (integration, prompt suite, eval harness)
- Redwood security liaison: Ben Carter (security checklist + SOC2 artifacts)
- Nimble account owner: Elena (POC success validation, product contact)

Proposed timeline (target dates)
- Confirm scope & security contacts: by 2026-07-03
- Data & test prompt handoff (Nimble -> Redwood): by 2026-07-06
- Integration + initial models live in staging: by 2026-07-13
- Soak & evaluation: 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-20
- Final review and next-steps: 2026-07-22

Next steps for us
- Marissa / Rishi: schedule technical scoping call with Elena + engineering (shared calendar stub below).
- Ben: share minimal security checklist; confirm encryption and audit log ask items.
- Elena: share 200-test-prompt sample and any retention constraints or PII redaction requirements.

Attachments: nimble_poc_scope_v1.pdf (scoping doc), test_prompt_suite.csv (sample prompts)

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on the scope and security contact and will get the scoping meeting on the calendar when I hear back.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC success matrix and model picks

Quick notes from a solutions perspective (to prepare for Tuesday’s scoping):
- Evaluation datasets: we’ll use Elena’s 200 redacted prompts + an internal 300-prompt challenge set that includes edge-case SKUs, return-policy queries, and multilingual paraphrases. Combined harness will run per-model and produce: BERTScore, BLEU, and a human-blind 5-point helpfulness rating.
- Latency testing: suggest synthetic load that mirrors expected production QPS with 50 concurrent sessions; capture token-level latency and end-to-end. Use Redwood’s continuous batching to approximate production latency.
- Quality gating: require OA-13B to beat Mistral-7b by at least 0.07 delta in BERTScore or show substantially fewer hallucinations on the SKU set to be accepted as primary. Otherwise, prefer Mistral for cost reasons.
- Multilingual handling: include translation consistency checks (EN->ES->EN roundtrip) and native PT-BR prompts from Nimble. We should instrument per-language metrics.
- Observability: we’ll create per-route dashboards for token usage, per-token latency, and a confusion matrix for entity extraction failures.

Deliverables before integration:
1) final test prompt CSV (Elena)
2) sample product catalog extraction spec (Nimble)
3) security checklist signed (Ben + Ana)

I’ll bring a short eval harness plan to the scoping call.

-Rishi
